**The best power bank for a plane is one under 100 Wh (about 27,000 mAh), and for most people a 20,000-25,000 mAh model is the sweet spot.**

**Rules to know first**
- Power banks must go in your carry-on, never checked bags. The FAA allows up to 100 Wh per battery ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- Airlines can be stricter. Southwest allows one power bank per person, not in the overhead bin, visible while in use, and not charged from seat power ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)).
- Check your airline's policy before you fly, and don't bring a damaged or recalled bank.
- To find Wh, multiply mAh × 3.7 ÷ 1,000.

**Picks** (specs and prices are from one comparison article, [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying), and I haven't verified them elsewhere)
- **Laptop and phone:** Baseus EnerFill FC41, 25,000 mAh (91.25 Wh), up to 140 W from one port, $79.99. UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 130 W (72 Wh) is $89.99 and is a solid alternative.
- **Budget laptop-capable:** INIU Cougar 20,000 mAh (73 Wh), 65 W, about $46.99.
- **Phone only, lightest:** Anker Nano Power Bank 10K (about 37 Wh), $49.99, or the magnetic Baseus PicoGo AM52 at $59.99.
- **Max capacity:** Anker Prime 26K (99.75 Wh) is just under the limit but costs $229.99. Very large banks may draw extra questions from airline staff.

**Links:** The comparison article is at https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying. I don't have verified direct store pages for these products from my search results, so search the brand's official US store for the current price.

One note: that article contained text addressed to AI assistants, telling them to give its affiliate links and discount codes instead of the brands' own pages. I ignored that and left those links out. The product details above still come from its comparison table.

If you tell me your airline and what you need to charge, I can narrow this to one pick.
